task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 gate (hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER) for ISS-0119. Verdict from the ARTEFACT ITSELF -- `lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md`, 737 lines. Do NOT validate from CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary; reading a producer's own summary and echoing it back is not validation (core-directives.md, 'Every producing step has a validating step').

The design chose BOTH remedies via a 'freeze-and-roll' scheme: close `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` in place as Volume 1 byte-identical through line 5,766, create `requirement_status.v2.yaml` as the current volume, and create a fixed-name `requirement_status.index.yaml` as the entry point every instruction site points at. Your job is to establish whether that design is correct, complete, and unambiguous enough to build from -- not whether it is the remedy you would have picked.

CHECK EACH OF THESE INDEPENDENTLY, and record a per-item verdict:

1. AC COVERAGE. The 12 acceptance criteria in `step-02-code-designer.json`'s task.acceptance_criteria. Map each to the specific design section that satisfies it. Any criterion with no concrete design element is a BLOCKER.

2. THE CENTRAL CLAIM IS ACTUALLY TRUE. The design asserts C4 is satisfied 'by construction' because Volume 1 is frozen in place, so `lib/letflow/design/iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367`'s citation of `requirement_status.yaml:5158` still resolves. VERIFY THIS YOURSELF: open that design doc at line 367, confirm what it actually cites, then confirm the design's freeze rule genuinely inserts nothing above line 5,766 -- including its own closure footer. If the footer is appended at EOF, state the current EOF line number and confirm 5,158 is unaffected. If any part of this does not hold, it is a BLOCKER: the whole justification for freeze-and-roll over a retroactive split rests on it.

3. THE HEADER PROCEDURE IS EXECUTABLE TODAY. §4 quotes the required new header in full and claims a six-step procedure with real commands for both shells. Read those commands and judge whether an agent could literally run them right now on this repo. Specifically: do they work on Windows/PowerShell AND bash (this repo runs both), do they depend on any tool not already present, and does the STOP-and-file fallback trigger on the real failure mode (a refused read) rather than on a hypothetical one? A procedure that is merely better-worded but still not runnable fails this gate -- that is the exact defect ISS-0119 is about.

4. THE APPEND-ONLY RULE IS NOT RELAXED. The design claims it strengthens the rule via assertion A6 (a sha256 over Volume 1's 5,766-line prefix). Confirm the design nowhere permits editing a past entry, and confirm A6 as specified would actually detect a retroactive edit. Check A6 is well-defined enough to implement: what exactly is hashed, with what line-ending handling. THIS REPO IS CRLF ON DISK AND LF IN GIT -- a hash spec that does not say which it covers is ambiguous and is at least a MAJOR issue, because the assertion would then pass or fail depending on checkout settings rather than on content.

5. THE 3 MALFORMED ENTRIES ARE HANDLED HONESTLY. Diagnosis constraint C2: nothing dropped, and the 3 `event: SCOPE-CHANGE` entries must NOT be silently normalized. The design claims A5 pins them in BOTH directions (new drift fails, later silent normalization also fails). Verify that is what §5 and §7 actually specify.

6. VOCABULARY COMPLETENESS. §5 must account for all 7 in-use `event` values (done 107, started 54, cancelled 8, blocked 5, revised 4, SCOPE-CHANGE 3, verified 1) and both `req` values. The design says 'exactly six legal values' for `event` while 7 are in use -- confirm the seventh is the 3 malformed entries being excluded by design and not an oversight. If any in-use value is silently dropped from the documented vocabulary without an explicit ruling, that is a BLOCKER, because the next append would then be told its own precedent is illegal.

7. THE 23 SITES ARE FULLY DISPOSITIONED. §10 claims 14 EDIT with post-edit text and 9 NO CHANGE with reasons. Count them. 14 + 9 = 23 must actually hold, each EDIT must carry text specific enough to apply without invention, and each NO CHANGE must carry a reason. Cross-check the site list against the Step 1 diagnosis's enumeration -- a site present in the diagnosis but missing from §10 is a BLOCKER.

8. THE PRECEDENCE RULING IS COHERENT. §9 rules that core-directives.md:173 (scoped reads) governs closed volumes and everything else, while the full read survives only for the CURRENT volume, bounded by the roll rule. Judge whether that is self-consistent and whether writing it in three places creates a restatement hazard this project otherwise avoids (its convention is one canonical home plus pointers).

9. NO IMPLEMENTATION LEAKED IN. The artefact is a design. Quoted required file content (the new header, replacement text for instruction sites) is legitimate and expected here -- that is the specification. What is NOT legitimate is the design having actually edited any of the target files. Verify with `git show --stat 24e7087` that the commit touched only the artefact and the handoff.

10. STEP 4 IS BUILDABLE. §7 proposes `test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs`, ExUnit, no DB, no new deps, 8 assertions, and claims A3 would have FAILED at commit 3d19e8c on 2026-08-18. Judge whether TEST-DESIGNER could write that file from §7 alone. The fail-first proof matters here: WF-03 Step 4 requires a test that fails pre-fix and passes post-fix, so confirm §7 gives TEST-DESIGNER a concrete way to demonstrate that.

11. OPEN QUESTIONS. §12 records 4, claiming none blocks Step 3. ORCH has accepted the defaults in #1, #2 and #4 as design decisions within CODE-DESIGNER's authority, and routes #3 (whether the invariant test should also be a standalone `mix letflow.check` step) to REVIEWER at Step 3d. Confirm none of the 4 in fact hides an unresolved decision ELIXIR-DEV would have to invent an answer to.

VERDICT RULES. PASS only if every check above passes. FAIL if any BLOCKER stands -- and on FAIL, name each gap by acceptance criterion with the specific missing element, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md §2's validator-fail worked example. Do not fix the design yourself and do not edit the artefact.
acceptance_criteria: The verdict is derived from lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md itself, and result.summary names the sections read
All 12 of Step 2's acceptance criteria are mapped to specific design sections, with any uncovered criterion raised as a BLOCKER
Check 2 is independently verified by opening iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367 and confirming the :5158 citation still resolves under the freeze rule
Check 3 states whether the header's commands are runnable today under both PowerShell and bash on this repo
Check 4 states whether A6's hash spec is unambiguous about CRLF-vs-LF, flagging at least MAJOR if not
Checks 5 and 6 confirm the 3 malformed entries are pinned without normalization and that all 7 in-use event values are explicitly accounted for
Check 7 verifies the 14 EDIT + 9 NO CHANGE sites sum to 23 and cross-checks them against the Step 1 diagnosis enumeration
Check 9 verifies via git show --stat 24e7087 that no target file was edited by the design step
Check 10 states whether TEST-DESIGNER could build the Step 4 test from §7 alone, including the fail-first demonstration
A per-item verdict is recorded for all 11 checks
The design artefact is not modified by this step

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 2 GATE VERDICT: **FAIL** (1 BLOCKER, 1 MAJOR, 3 MINOR). Rework to CODE-DESIGNER; rework_count 0 -> 1 of 3.

Verdict derived from the artefact, not from CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary. Sections read in full: title block, S1 (decision), S2 (target layout), S3.1/3.2/3.3 (exact per-file changes incl. both quoted new files), S4 (the quoted volume header, all six HOW-TO-APPEND steps, both vocabulary blocks, the roll rule), S5 (vocabulary/anomalies), S6 (growth threshold), S7 (A1-A8), S8 (no-entry-dropped + 6 verification commands), S9 (precedence ruling), S10.1-10.6 (all 24 site rows + every replacement text), S11 (file list), S12 (4 open questions). Cross-read: step-01 diagnosis result.summary sections 0-5, step-02 handoff task.acceptance_criteria, core-directives.md, HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md S1/S2/S4, WF-03 Step 4.

The design is strong and mostly buildable. It fails on exactly the thing ISS-0119 is about: one step of its own "executable" procedure is not executable on this host's primary shell.

=== PER-ITEM VERDICTS (11/11 recorded) ===

CHECK 1 - AC COVERAGE: FAIL (1 of 12 uncovered). Mapping:
 AC1 -> title block + verified by git show (check 9). PASS.
 AC2 -> S1 "Why not (b) alone" / "Why not (a) alone" / "Why both" - each justified by direct quotation of the Step 1 diagnosis (C7, the 2026-08-17 L2 finding, the "multiplies the L2 problem" warning), not ISS-0119 prose. PASS.
 AC3 -> S9 + S10.3. PASS.
 AC4 -> S1 final para, S7 A6, S10.2 (doc-updater :47). PASS.
 AC5 -> S3, S10.2-10.6, S11. PASS.
 AC6 (conditional) -> boundary/roll rule S6, index structure S3.3, fate of original path S2+S3.1, :5158 resolution S8, no-entry-dropped method + 6 verification commands S8. PASS.
 AC7 -> S4. **BLOCKER, see check 3.** Header text is quoted in full (that half is satisfied); the "executable today as concrete commands" half is not.
 AC8 -> S4 vocabulary blocks + S5 table. PASS.
 AC9 -> S10.4. PASS.
 AC10 -> S6. PASS.
 AC11 -> S7 (test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs, A1-A8). PASS on the letter; see check 10 MAJOR.
 AC12 -> verified by git show (check 9). PASS.

CHECK 2 - THE CENTRAL CLAIM: **PASS, independently verified.**
 - lib/letflow/design/iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367 reads verbatim: "  `docs/status/requirement_status.yaml:5158`," - it sits inside the "Prose-only references, not call sites" bullet. Citation confirmed, by line number, exactly as the design describes.
 - sed -n '5158p' docs/status/requirement_status.yaml returns "      merge_effective_pins, returning a distinct UnknownPinRef and" - inside the note: prose of the REQ-059/PIN-05 entry. The design's structural claim is accurate.
 - wc -l docs/status/requirement_status.yaml = 5766. Current EOF line = 5766, matching the design's frozen-prefix figure exactly. The S3.1 footer is specified as an append "after the current last line (5,766)", "Nothing above line 5,766 may be touched". An append at EOF inserts only at 5767+, so line 5,158 does not move. C4 holds by construction; :5158 still resolves. Nothing in S3.1, S3.2, S3.3 or S10 writes above line 5,766, and S10 explicitly forbids editing iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367.

CHECK 3 - HEADER PROCEDURE EXECUTABLE TODAY: **FAIL - BLOCKER.**
 S4 opens with the absolute claim "Every command below is runnable today on this repo." That claim is false on this host's primary shell, and I verified it rather than reasoning about it. Ran in PowerShell: `grep --version` -> "The term 'grep' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program." CommandNotFoundException.
 S4 HOW-TO-APPEND step 1 is the only step of the procedure given as a single unlabelled command, and it is a GNU-grep invocation:
     grep -n 'status: current' -B 2 docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml
 Steps 2, 3 and the roll-rule block are correctly given as labelled Bash/PowerShell pairs; step 5 (`git diff --numstat`) is genuinely cross-shell. So the author knew the both-shells requirement and step 1 is the omission.
 Consequence: a DOC-UPDATER turn on PowerShell hits a CommandNotFoundException on the FIRST step of the procedure whose entire purpose is to be executable, and must improvise a substitute unaided - the identical failure shape the Step 1 diagnosis documented ("no written rule tells it what to do next... it must invent a substitute unaided"). This is ISS-0119 reproduced inside ISS-0119's own fix. It is not a wording nit; a hard gate that lets this through leaves the mechanism unexecutable for half the sessions that run it.
 STOP-and-file fallback: this part is CORRECT and triggers on the real failure mode - S4 step 2 says "If that read is refused or truncated, STOP: the roll rule has failed and that is itself a defect to file, not to work around", and S10.3's core-directives.md:328 replacement repeats it with ISS-0119 named as precedent. That is the refusal, not a hypothetical.
 No new tooling is required anywhere else in the procedure: git, wc, sed, Get-Item, Get-Content and Get-Date are all present.
 REQUIRED FIX (one line, no redesign): give step 1 a labelled shell pair as steps 2/3 already do, e.g.
     Bash:       grep -n 'status: current' -B 2 docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml
     PowerShell: Select-String -Path docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml -Pattern 'status: current' -Context 2,0
 and sweep S10.2/S10.3's prose ("targeted grep/sed", "read those with grep/sed/awk only") for the same assumption - core-directives.md:156-161 already sets the both-shells precedent this repo follows.

CHECK 4 - APPEND-ONLY NOT RELAXED: **PASS.** Nothing in the artefact permits editing a past entry. The prohibition is stated affirmatively in S1 ("Nothing in this design permits rewriting any past entry, in any volume, ever"), S3.1 (footer: "Nothing here is rewritten, corrected, renumbered or moved"), S3.3 (index header: "appended, never edited, never reordered, never deleted, in any volume, closed or current"), S4 (header: "NEVER REWRITE, REORDER, EDIT OR DELETE A PAST ENTRY"), S10.2 (doc-updater :47 extension to every volume), S10.3 and S10.5. The rule is strengthened, not relaxed: it gains its first mechanical enforcement.
 A6 would detect a retroactive edit: SHA-256 over volume 1's first 5,766 lines covers every one of the 182 entries, so any character change inside the frozen prefix changes the digest and fails the suite. The footer is deliberately placed beyond the prefix so it can be written once without invalidating the digest - that is coherent.
 CRLF-vs-LF: **UNAMBIGUOUS, criterion satisfied.** Stated identically in three places - S3.3 index comment "SHA-256 of lines 1..5766 with CRLF normalised to LF, i.e. the frozen prefix"; S7 A6 "(CRLF normalized to LF, so the digest is platform-stable)"; S8 step 5 "Compute frozen_prefix_sha256 over lines 1-5766 with CRLF normalized to LF". This repo is CRLF on disk / LF in git (diagnosis section 0: blob 355,610 LF bytes vs 361,376 working-tree bytes), and the spec names which one it covers, so the assertion is checkout-independent. Not flagged as MAJOR. One MINOR residue below (trailing-terminator handling).
 Note the design correctly does NOT apply the same normalisation to the roll rule, which deliberately measures the WORKING TREE ("because that is what the Read tool measures", S3.3 + S4 + S6). Two different measurements for two different purposes, each stated - self-consistent.

CHECK 5 - THE 3 MALFORMED ENTRIES: **PASS.** S5 specifies four dispositions: not edited ("Not in this run, not ever"), not hidden (declared in volume 1's footer S3.1, the index's known_anomalies: S3.3, and the current volume's header S4), attributed (each declaration names TASK_QUEUE.md:133 as cause), machine-pinned. S7 A5 pins both directions verbatim: "A new violation fails (drift detected); a missing one fails (a past entry was silently normalized or deleted)". S3.3's known_anomalies: carries all three (3490/REQ-031, 3577/REQ-042, 3744/REQ-038) with path, line, field, value, should_have_been and cause. S8 verification step 4 (`sed -n '3490p;3577p;3744p'` must still return three `event: SCOPE-CHANGE` lines) makes the non-normalisation checkable at Step 3, before the test even exists. S10.2's doc-updater :47 text forbids "cleaning up" them by name. Diagnosis C2 is satisfied in the strong form.

CHECK 6 - VOCABULARY COMPLETENESS: **PASS.** S5's table accounts for all 7 in-use event values with the diagnosis's exact counts (done 107, started 54, cancelled 8, blocked 5, revised 4, verified 1, SCOPE-CHANGE 3). The seventh is an EXPLICIT RULING, not an oversight: S4 states "SCOPE-CHANGE IS NOT AN EVENT VALUE. Three volume-1 entries (lines 3490, 3577, 3744) carry `event: SCOPE-CHANGE`. They are wrong, they are recorded as known anomalies in the index, and they are LEFT AS WRITTEN". So the next append is never told its own precedent is illegal without also being told why and where the exception is recorded. Both req: values covered (REQ-NNN 151, SCOPE-CHANGE 31), plus an explicit zero-precedent ruling that `req: ISS-NNNN` is illegal - which directly pre-empts the wrong guess this very run would otherwise make at Step 6. S4 also states the extension procedure for a seventh value (amend the header in the same commit that first uses it), so vocabulary growth is not left to improvisation.

CHECK 7 - THE 23 SITES: **PASS on substance; the handoff's own 14+9 figure is wrong.** Counted mechanically over S10.1: 25 table lines = 1 header + 24 data rows; 16 rows marked **EDIT**, 8 marked NO CHANGE. The 23 NUMBERED rows are 15 EDIT + 8 NO CHANGE = 23; the 24th row is the unnumbered `core-directives.md:173` back-reference EDIT the design adds on top of the diagnosis's list. So the correct arithmetic is 15+8=23 numbered sites (16 EDITs including the added one), not 14+9. The set is complete and correctly totalled - only the count quoted in this handoff's task text (inherited from the producer's summary) is off. Recorded MINOR.
 Cross-check against diagnosis section 3(ii) items 1-23: 1:1, same file and same line for every one (CLAUDE.md:85; core-directives :290/:328/:354; doc-updater :17/:23/:31/:47; release-validator :23/:32; AGENT_SYSTEM :46/:105/:136; ORCHESTRATOR :129; WF-01:59; WF-02 :106/:377/:390; WF-04:66; ISSUE_QUEUE:156; TASK_QUEUE :133/:379; anti-patterns :68-83). No diagnosis site is missing.
 Every one of the 16 EDITs carries applicable post-edit text: S10.2 (doc-updater :17/:31/:47), S10.3 (core-directives :328 and :173), S10.4 (TASK_QUEUE :133/:379), S10.5 (anti-patterns rewrite + a new entry), S10.6 (CLAUDE.md:85, core-directives:290, release-validator:23, AGENT_SYSTEM :46/:105/:136, WF-02 :106/:390). AGENT_SYSTEM :46/:136 are given as a cell-level instruction ("widen to docs/status/requirement_status*.yaml (index + all volumes), owner DOC-UPDATER") rather than a full quoted row - specific enough to apply without invention. Every one of the 8 NO CHANGE rows carries a reason. The design also dispositions diagnosis section 3(i) prose referrers, including requirements.yaml:444 (left as-is, resolved through the index) and iss-0078-pin-rebind-provenance.md:367 (must NOT be edited).

CHECK 8 - PRECEDENCE RULING: **PASS, with a MINOR restatement hazard.** Self-consistent: :173 (scoped reads) is the general rule governing closed volumes and every other large file; the full read survives only for the CURRENT volume and only because the roll rule bounds it - and S10.3 closes the loop by ruling that a refused full read of the current volume is a roll-rule defect to file, not a licence to append from a fragment. That last clause is what makes the ruling non-circular; without it the exception would re-open the same gap on the next threshold.
 On the restatement convention: three sites is acceptable here and does not violate one-canonical-home-plus-pointers - S9 names :328 as "the primary statement", :173 as "a back-reference", and the index header as the entry point, i.e. one home and two pointers. Carrying the schema into every volume header is required by the diagnosis itself (a split without it "multiplies the L2 problem").
 MINOR hazard: the numeric ceilings 1,200 lines / 120,000 bytes are written out in FIVE places (index roll_rule, every volume header, core-directives:328 replacement, doc-updater.md:31 replacement, anti-patterns.md replacement), while A3 reads them only from the index and A8 checks only that the header names the vocabulary - not the ceilings. Changing a ceiling later would leave up to four prose copies stale with nothing to detect it. Recorded MINOR; a natural fix is an A8 extension asserting the header's quoted ceilings match roll_rule, or replacing the prose numbers with a pointer to the index.

CHECK 9 - NO IMPLEMENTATION LEAKED IN: **PASS, verified.** `git show --stat 24e7087` returns exactly two files: handoffs/WF03-ISS0119-20260821/step-02-code-designer.json (74 +) and lib/letflow/design/iss-0119-status-file-readability.md (737 +), "2 files changed, 811 insertions(+)". No target file was edited - docs/status/requirement_status.yaml, the index, v2, core-directives.md, doc-updater.md, TASK_QUEUE.md, anti-patterns.md and all remaining instruction sites are untouched by the design step. Confirmed independently: `git status --porcelain` on this branch shows no modification to any of them. The verbatim file content in S3.1/S3.3/S4/S10 is specification, which the handoff sanctions; it is quoted inside fenced blocks in the design, not written to the target paths. AC1 and AC12 satisfied.

CHECK 10 - STEP 4 BUILDABLE: **PARTIAL - MAJOR.** A1-A8 are individually buildable from S7 alone: ExUnit, no DB, no new deps, :crypto for the digest, index-derived volume list, and the entry/field grammar is stated ("entries start with `  - req: ` and fields with four-space indent"). A3's inputs are fully concrete (File.stat! bytes vs roll_rule.max_bytes, line count vs roll_rule.max_lines). TEST-DESIGNER can write the file.
 What is MISSING is the fail-first mechanism, which WF-03 Step 4 requires explicitly: "Step 4's test must be shown to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the post-fix code... (checked out the pre-fix commit, ran the new test, confirms it failed)". S7 asserts A3 "would have failed on 2026-08-18 at commit 3d19e8c" - a counterfactual that is arithmetically well-founded (the diagnosis measured 4,217 lines / 264,861 working-tree bytes there, over both ceilings) but is NOT a runnable demonstration, because every assertion including A3 is derived from docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml, and that file does not exist at 3d19e8c or at any pre-fix commit. Checking out the pre-fix tree and running the test yields a missing-index error, not an A3 size failure - a failure that any test of any new file would produce, and which therefore proves nothing about whether the test covers this bug (the precise objection WF-03 Step 4 raises).
 S7 names no way to close this. TEST-DESIGNER would have to invent one - a fixture index under test/fixtures/ pointing at a copy of the pre-fix file, an A3 size-check helper callable against an arbitrary path, or `git show 3d19e8c:docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` piped into a temp file. Which of those is chosen changes the test's shape, so it is a design decision, not a mechanical detail. REQUIRED FIX: S7 states the fail-first procedure concretely - which artefact stands in for the pre-fix state, where it lives, and how A3 is exercised against it - so TEST-DESIGNER can demonstrate a MEANINGFUL failure rather than a missing-file failure.

CHECK 11 - OPEN QUESTIONS: **PASS.** None hides an unresolved decision ELIXIR-DEV must invent an answer to. #1 (volume naming) states the choice made (.v2.yaml), its reason, and that nothing depends on it because every consumer goes through the index - a made decision with an alternative recorded. #2 (ceilings) states the chosen values, their derivation from the tool limits, and a hard constraint on any change ("must never be raised to the tool limits themselves") - decided, with a guardrail. #3 (standalone `mix letflow.check` step) is correctly framed as additive: the test runs under plain `mix test` either way, so Step 3 is unblocked regardless of REVIEWER's answer at 3d. #4 (anomalies permanent) is a decision taken, not deferred, and names the only append-only-compatible future route. Separately, S11's "Step 4 may own the test instead, at ORCH's routing discretion; the design specifies it either way" is a routing question, not a design gap - the file path and contents are pinned regardless of who writes it.

=== WHAT REWORK MUST DO (minimal, no redesign) ===
1. [BLOCKER, AC7] S4 HOW-TO-APPEND step 1: replace the bare grep with a labelled Bash/PowerShell pair (grep is verified absent from PowerShell on this host), and sweep S10.2/S10.3's grep/sed prose for the same assumption.
2. [MAJOR, WF-03 Step 4] S7: specify the concrete fail-first procedure for A3 against the pre-fix state, given the test is index-driven and no index exists pre-fix.
3. [MINOR] S8/S3.3: state whether the frozen-prefix digest includes a trailing line terminator after line 5,766 (join-with-LF vs terminate-with-LF give different digests; harmless today because ELIXIR-DEV pastes whatever the test computes, but it should be written down, since the digest's whole job is to be reproducible by a later agent).
4. [MINOR] S11: "Modified (10)" enumerates 9 distinct files (requirement_status.yaml, CLAUDE.md, core-directives.md, doc-updater.md, release-validator.md, AGENT_SYSTEM.md, WF-02, TASK_QUEUE.md, anti-patterns.md). The list is exhaustive; only the count is wrong. Fix the count so ELIXIR-DEV's own file-count check at Step 3 does not disagree with the design.
5. [MINOR] S8/S4 step 2: the two commands given measure size, and the Bash form reports lines only while the PowerShell form reports bytes only, although step 2 states both bounds. Give both measurements in both shells, as the roll-rule block already does.
Not blocking, recorded for the source: this handoff's task text says S10 claims "14 EDIT and 9 NO CHANGE"; the artefact's table is 15 EDIT + 8 NO CHANGE over 23 numbered sites (16 EDIT over 24 rows, including the added core-directives.md:173 back-reference). All 23 diagnosis sites are present, so the design is not at fault - the figure came from the producer's summary.

The artefact was not modified by this step; the only file this step writes is its own handoff.

issues.description: AC7 ("the procedure the header prescribes is executable today as concrete commands") is not met. Section 4's HOW-TO-APPEND step 1 is a bare GNU-grep invocation -- `grep -n 'status: current' -B 2 docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml` -- given without a shell label, while steps 2, 3 and the roll-rule block are correctly given as Bash/PowerShell pairs. Verified empirically on this host, not inferred: running `grep --version` in PowerShell returns "The term 'grep' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet, function, script file, or operable program" (CommandNotFoundException). Section 4 nevertheless opens with "Every command below is runnable today on this repo." A DOC-UPDATER turn on PowerShell therefore fails on the FIRST step of the procedure whose entire purpose is executability, and must improvise a substitute unaided -- the exact failure shape the Step 1 diagnosis documented and the exact defect ISS-0119 exists to remove. MISSING ELEMENT: a PowerShell form for step 1, e.g. `Select-String -Path docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml -Pattern 'status: current' -Context 2,0`, following the both-shells precedent core-directives.md:156-161 already sets; plus a sweep of Sections 10.2 and 10.3's "targeted grep/sed" and "grep/sed/awk only" prose for the same assumption.

Section 7 does not give TEST-DESIGNER a way to demonstrate the fail-first property WF-03 Step 4 requires ("the test must be shown to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the post-fix code... checked out the pre-fix commit, ran the new test, confirms it failed"). Section 7 states every assertion is "derived from the index file so the test never hardcodes a volume list", but docs/status/requirement_status.index.yaml does not exist at commit 3d19e8c or at any pre-fix commit. Running the new test on the pre-fix tree therefore errors on a missing index rather than failing A3's size check -- a failure any test of any new file would produce, proving nothing about coverage of this bug. The claim that "A3 would have failed on 2026-08-18 at commit 3d19e8c" is arithmetically sound (the diagnosis measured 4,217 lines / 264,861 working-tree bytes there, over both ceilings) but is a counterfactual, not a runnable demonstration. MISSING ELEMENT: a concrete fail-first procedure in Section 7 -- which artefact stands in for the pre-fix state (fixture index under test/fixtures/, an A3 size-check helper callable against an arbitrary path, or `git show 3d19e8c:docs/status/requirement_status.yaml` into a temp file), where it lives, and how A3 is exercised against it. The choice changes the test's shape, so it is a design decision TEST-DESIGNER must not have to invent.

Section 8 step 5 and Section 3.3 specify frozen_prefix_sha256 as "SHA-256 over lines 1-5766 with CRLF normalized to LF" -- unambiguous about line endings (criterion satisfied, not flagged MAJOR) but silent on whether a trailing line terminator follows line 5,766 in the hashed byte stream.
